Compare two scenarios' model inputs

Source: R/compare_inputs.R
compare_inputs.Rd

Mechanically diffs the interpolated model input (modInp) of two scenarios: parameter presence, per-parameter metadata (dimSets – distinguishing order-only changes – type, defVal, interpolation, desc), parameter data (key-based, row-order insensitive, with numeric tolerance), model sets, the compiled user constraints / user cost terms, and @misc. The classic use is explaining WHY two solved scenarios differ, or guarding a refactor of the interpolation pipeline.

Usage

compare_inputs(a, b, tol = 1e-08, unfold = FALSE, names = c("A", "B"))

# S3 method for class 'inputs_cmp'
print(x, max_diffs = 5L, ...)

Arguments

a, b

scenario or modInp objects.

tol

numeric, absolute tolerance for value comparisons.

unfold

logical, unfold folded parameters before comparing (scenario inputs only).

names

character(2), display names of the two sides.

x

an inputs_cmp object.

max_diffs

integer, number of differing parameters to render with a detailed waldo diff (when waldo is installed).

...

ignored.

Value

An inputs_cmp object (a list) with components names, summary (one row per common parameter: parameter, status, n_A, n_B, n_diff, max_abs_diff, meta; status is one of identical, meta-diff, value-diff, rows-mismatch, rows-only-A, rows-only-B, structural, diff), params (only_A / only_B / common with per-parameter detail), sets, equations, misc, and tol. print() gives a compact report; with waldo installed it renders textual diffs for the first differing parameters.

Details

Data is compared as stored by default; unfold = TRUE collapses fold-vs-dense representation drift first (requires scenario inputs).

See also

compare_scenarios() for solved-results comparison, compare_models() for declaration-level model diffs.

Other comparison: compare_models(), compare_scenarios()

Examples

# \donttest{
ek  <- topia$modules$electricity$R3
mod <- newModel("TOPIA", data = ek$repo,
                calendar = topia$modules$calendars$s4_h24,
                region = ek$regions,
                horizon = topia$modules$horizons$base,
                discount = 0.05)
mod <- setGeoscale(mod, ek$geoscale)

# the same model with a three-step gas supply curve instead of flat supply
mod2 <- add(mod, ek$GAS_CURVE, overwrite = TRUE)
a <- interpolate_model(mod,  name = "FLAT")
#> Cost declared at a coarse geoscale level:
#>   TBD_COA_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#>   TBD_GAS_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#> The cost is charged ONCE at that cell rather than at each child region, and is discounted at the children's rate. That is usually what a national cost datum means -- said here because it is a different number from naming the children individually.
b <- interpolate_model(mod2, name = "CURVE")
#> Cost declared at a coarse geoscale level:
#>   TBD_COA_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#>   TBD_GAS_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#> The cost is charged ONCE at that cell rather than at each child region, and is discounted at the children's rate. That is usually what a national cost datum means -- said here because it is a different number from naming the children individually.

cmp <- compare_inputs(a, b, names = c("flat", "curve"))
cmp
